'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[War in Afghanistan (2001–present)|War in Afghanistan]]
**[[Taliban insurgency]]
***[[2021 Taliban offensive]]
****[[India]]n [[Reuters]] photojournalist [[Danish Siddiqui]] is killed while covering a clash between the [[Taliban]] and Afghan government forces on the border with [[Pakistan]]. A senior Afghan officer is also killed in the attack. Reuters president [[Michael Friedenberg]] and [[editor-in-chief]] [[Alessandra Galloni]] say that they are urgently seeking information with authorities in the region. Reports by the government indicate that Siddiqui was killed in Taliban crossfire. [https://www.reuters.com/world/asia-pacific/reuters-journalist-killed-covering-clash-between-afghan-forces-taliban-2021-07-16/ (Reuters)]
**Pakistan rejects accusations by the [[Vice President of Afghanistan|Afghan first vice-president]] [[Amrullah Saleh]] that the [[Pakistan Air Force|Pakistani Air Force]] provides air support to the Taliban. Pakistani authorities rebuffed the accusation on Friday, saying that the [[Air Force]] limits itself to safeguarding Pakistani territory. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/7/16/pakistan-air-support-afghanistan-taliban (Al Jazeera)]

'''Arts and culture'''
*[[Impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on tourism]], [[Impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on the arts and cultural heritage]], [[COVID-19 pandemic in France]]
**The [[Eiffel Tower]] reopens to tourists after a nearly nine-month closure due to the second wave of the pandemic and renovations, which is the longest closure since [[World War II]]. However, all visitors over 18 years of age will need to show a Health Pass proving that they have been fully vaccinated, tested negative, or recovered from [[COVID-19]] beginning July 21. [https://apnews.com/article/europe-health-coronavirus-pandemic-c9e8cf1c25e0245ef65f4b9f9a01a82e (AP)] 

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*[[2021 European floods]]
**The death toll from the severe floods in western [[Germany]] increases to 133. Ninety people died in [[Rhineland-Palatinate]] and 43 died in [[North Rhine-Westphalia]]. The death toll in [[Belgium]] also increases to 27. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/7/16/rescuers-rush-to-help-as-europes-flood-toll-surpasses-125 (Al Jazeera)]
*[[2021 Madagascar food crisis]]
**[[Malagasy President]] [[Andry Rajoelina]] pleads to world leaders and the international community to help combat [[climate change]] amid a situation of [[food insecurity]] with some people on the verge of [[famine]] in the southern region of [[Madagascar]]. Rajoelina highlights the "urgency" in addressing the issue. [https://www.madagascar-tribune.com/Andry-Rajoelina-plaide-en-faveur-des-victimes-du-changement-climatique.html (''Madagascar Tribune'')]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Asia]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Israel]]
****[[Travel restrictions related to the COVID-19 pandemic]]
*****The [[Ministry of Health (Israel)|Ministry of Health]] announces that all travel to [[Spain]] and [[Kyrgyzstan]] will be banned amid an increase in the number of [[COVID-19]] cases. The order will be in effect on July 23. [https://en.trend.az/world/israel/3456636.html (Trend)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Indonesia]]
****[[Indonesia]] reports a record 1,205 deaths from COVID-19 in the past 24 hours, 345 of them from [[East Java]], thereby bringing the nationwide death toll to 71,397. [https://www.liputan6.com/health/read/4608918/1205-orang-meninggal-karena-covid-19-jatim-capai-345-per-16-juli-2021 (Liputan6)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the Philippines]]
****The [[Philippines]] reports its first death and first locally transmitted cases from the [[SARS-CoV-2 Delta variant]] in 11 people that were locally infected with the variant and one person who died at a hospital in [[Manila]] on June 28. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/7/16/philippines-confirms-first-case-of-delta-variant (Al Jazeera English)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Sri Lanka]], [[COVID-19 vaccination in Sri Lanka]]
****[[Sri Lanka]] receives its first shipment of 1.5 million doses of the [[Moderna COVID-19 vaccine]] from the [[United States]]. [http://www.dailynews.lk/2021/07/16/local/254154/sri-lanka-receives-first-batch-moderna-vaccine (Daily News)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Thailand]]
****[[Thailand]] reports a record 9,692 new cases of COVID-19 in the past 24 hours, thereby bringing the nationwide total of confirmed cases to 381,907. [https://www.channelnewsasia.com/news/asia/covid-19-thailand-record-daily-number-cases-infections-15230934 (CNA)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Vietnam]]
****[[Vietnam]] surpasses 40,000 cases of COVID-19. [https://e.vnexpress.net/news/news/vietnam-s-new-wave-covid-19-tally-crosses-40-000-4325991.html (VN Express)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Europe]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Greece]]
****[[Greece]] imposes new restrictions for access to the hospitality and entertainment sectors to those who have been vaccinated or who have recovered from COVID-19, particularly for those who want to visit indoor spaces like restaurants, bars and cafés. [https://greekreporter.com/2021/07/16/greece-imposes-new-rules-covid-free-restaurants-cafes-bars/ (Greek Reporter)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Russia]]
****[[Russia]] reports a record for the fourth consecutive day of 799 deaths from COVID-19, thereby bringing the nationwide death toll to 146,868. [https://m.timesofindia.com/world/rest-of-world/russia-reports-record-daily-covid-19-deaths-for-fourth-day-running/amp_articleshow/84468583.cms (''The Times of India'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Spain]]
****[[Queen Letizia of Spain|Queen consort Letizia]] and heir presumptive [[Leonor, Princess of Asturias]] receive the first dose of the vaccine. [https://www.elmundo.es/loc/casa-real/2021/07/16/60f1791ee4d4d8987b8b468d.html (''El Mundo'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United Kingdom]]
****The [[United Kingdom]] reports 51,870 new cases of COVID-19 in the past 24 hours, which is the first time that the country has reported more than 50,000 cases since January 15. [https://www.bbc.com/news/uk-57867990 (BBC News)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Africa]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Namibia]]
****[[Namibia]] receives a shipment of 250,000 doses of the [[Sinopharm]] [[BBIBP-CorV]] vaccine from [[China]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/africa/vaccine-starved-namibia-receives-sinopharm-boost-2021-07-16/ (Reuters)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Tunisia]]
****[[Tunisia]] reports a record 205 deaths from COVID-19 in the past 24 hours, taking the death toll to 17,214 deaths. The country also faces shortage of oxygen as hospital struggle with collapse. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/7/17/tunisia-marks-worse-daily-covid-deaths-since-start-of-pandemic (Al Jazeera)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Zimbabwe]]
****[[Zimbabwe]] reports a record for the fourth consecutive day of 86 deaths from COVID-19, thereby bringing the nationwide death toll to 2,418. [https://www.aa.com.tr/en/africa/zimbabwe-confirms-record-daily-covid-19-deaths/2306890 (Anadolu Agency)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Oceania]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Australia]]
****The state of [[Victoria (Australia)|Victoria]] enters a [[COVID-19 lockdowns|lockdown]] for the fifth time since the pandemic began, after experiencing an increase in COVID-19 cases spreading south from the [[New South Wales]] outbreak. [https://www.theguardian.com/australia-news/2021/jul/15/victoria-covid-update-state-set-to-go-into-lockdown-as-clusters-linked-to-sydney-outbreak-grow (''The Guardian'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Papua New Guinea]]
****Authorities in [[Papua New Guinea]] urge people to get vaccinated as the first case of the [[SARS-CoV-2 Delta variant]] was confirmed yesterday in the Filipino captain of a ship which was docked in [[Port Moresby]]. Currently less than 1% of Papuans are vaccinated. [https://www.rnz.co.nz/international/pacific-news/447015/delta-variant-confirmed-in-png (RNZ)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United States]]
***[[COVID-19 vaccination in the United States]]
****The [[United States|U.S.]] [[Food and Drug Administration]] says that it has granted priority review for [[Pfizer–BioNTech COVID-19 vaccine|the vaccine]] developed by [[Pfizer]] and [[BioNTech]]. A decision on whether to fully approve the vaccine will likely be made within two months. [https://www.nydailynews.com/coronavirus/ny-covid-fda-full-approval-pfizer-20210716-qpzyfvmbp5eyzd4mbgg2otafga-story.html (''New York Daily News'')]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Argentina]]
***[[Argentina]] begins a five-day mourning period, decreed yesterday by [[President of Argentina|President]] [[Alberto Fernández]], to honor the more than 100,000 deaths from COVID-19 in the country. All flags are ordered to fly at half-mast. [https://en.mercopress.com/2021/07/16/argentine-government-decrees-five-days-of-mourning-for-victims-of-covid-19 (MercoPress)]
*The [[Centers for Disease Control and Prevention|U.S. CDC]] reports the first case of [[monkeypox]] in a [[Texas]] resident who traveled from [[Nigeria]]. [https://www.washingtonpost.com/health/2021/07/16/monkeypox-case-flight-dallas/ (''The Washington Post'')]

'''International relations'''
*[[China–United States relations]], [[2021 arrests of Hong Kong pro-democracy primaries participants]]
**The United States [[United States Treasury Department|Department of the Treasury]] sanctions eight Chinese officials over the crackdown on Hong Kong pro-democracy activists amid a trial of 47 of them on charges of "subverting state power". [https://www.reuters.com/world/asia-pacific/us-sanctions-seven-chinese-individuals-over-hong-kong-crackdown-2021-07-16/ (Reuters)]

'''Law and crime'''
*Human rights organizations file criminal complaints against 25 [[El Salvador|Salvadoran]] soldiers for the killings of four Dutch journalists during the [[Salvadoran Civil War|country's civil war]] in 1982. The journalists worked for the Dutch broadcaster [[Interkerkelijke Omroep Nederland]]. [https://www.swissinfo.ch/eng/salvadoran-soldiers-charged-with-deaths-of-four-dutch-reporters-in-1982/46793734 (SwissInfo)]
*[[Thailand|Thai]] [[Ministry of Justice (Thailand)|Minister for Justice]] [[Somsak Thepsuthin]] announces that the cultivation and export of [[Mitragyna speciosa|kratom]] will be legalized in the country on August 24, barring any constitutional objections. It was previously declassified as an illegal drug in May. [https://www.bangkokpost.com/thailand/general/2149423/kratom-plants-legal-to-grow-from-aug-24 (''Bangkok Post'')]

'''Science and technology'''
*The [[Hubble Space Telescope]] is successfully brought back online after a hardware failure with its payload computer on June 13, which left it unable to perform scientific operations for more than a month. [https://www.space.com/hubble-space-telescope-backup-hardware-success (Space.com)]
